text:
Alex: Heads up — noticed a regression in perceived streaming latency after last night's kernel-selector change on canary. p99 tokens-to-first-byte spiked for short prompts, users reporting stutter. Dumping quick notes.
Mira: Which selector tweak was that? the short-seq fused path?

Alex: Yes — we flipped preference to fused_int8 for seq<=128 to improve throughput. Throughput looks better but first-token times are worse for tail. Quick metrics (canary):
- before: p50 45ms, p95 110ms, p99 200ms
- after:  p50 48ms, p95 140ms, p99 420ms

Jon: Wow p99 doubled. Did microbatching or flush intervals change too?

Alex: We also changed microbatch default from 8 -> 12 to raise GPU utilization. Flush interval stayed at 40ms. Suspect interaction: larger microbatches + longer wait -> head-of-line + KV window growth.

Zane: Any change in KV cache hit rate / evictions?

Alex: Yes — KV hit-rate on canary for small prompts dropped 98.6% -> 96.1%. Queue wait times increased. Attaching profiler summary below.

profiling-bot: https://perf.internal/fg/1792004321 (flamegraph link)

Mira: Paste the hot path lines?

Alex: ````
# flame top 10 (simplified)
1  fused_int8_kernel (time slices)
2  memcpy_weights -> align_fixup
3  assemble_request_batch
4  wait_for_batch_start
5  kv_cache_lookup -> miss -> reload_prefix
6  stream_chunk_flush
````

Jon: memcpy_weights + align_fixup smells like an extra copy for the fused path. For small microbatches that copy overhead dominates and creates tail spikes.

Alex: Re-ran a quick param sweep on canary:
- microbatch=4, flush=20ms, chunk_tokens=8  -> p99 ~ 230ms
- microbatch=8, flush=40ms, chunk_tokens=16 -> p99 ~ 310ms
- microbatch=12, flush=40ms, chunk_tokens=32 -> p99 ~ 420ms
So both microbatch size and chunk token size amplify the tail.

Mira: Sounds like two interacting causes: (A) fused kernel path introduces fixed-copy overhead per batch, (B) larger microbatches increase per-request queuing and broaden KV windows (more misses).

Zane: For KV: larger microbatches can cause different request coalescing that reduces prefix reuse — more miss-induced reloads => extra latency. We should instrument per-request kv_window_size and eviction_count.

Alex: Action items I propose:
- revert the fused_int8 preference for seq<=64 on canary (quick rollback)
- run AB grid of microbatch x flush x chunk_tokens for short prompts (<=128)
- add queue_wait_ms and kv_window_size to streaming dashboard
- add unit test in microbatch-sim for KV windowing behavior

Jon: Also add a mitigation: dynamic flush interval — smaller flush for short prompt streaming (15-25ms) and normal 40ms for long prompts. That reduces perceived latency while keeping throughput in steady state.

Mira: Agree. Also check routing fallback: if fused kernel unstable, some requests are routed to CPU fallback path which hugely increases tail. Make sure fallback counts are in the canary alert.

deploy-bot: deploy request queued: deploy/rollout/1792004401 (canary revert)

Alex: Quick patch: lowered default flush to 25ms for streaming small prompts as a short-term mitigation. Will monitor.

profiling-bot: canary redeploy finished at 1792004470, id=deploy-1792004470

Alex: Early after rollback numbers: p99 down to ~260ms (better but not baseline). Running full sweep now.

Zane: If rollback doesn't fully return baseline, we should consider a micro-optimization: avoid memcpy by aligning fused kernel entry for small batches or use sticky weight pointers.

Jon: +1 on sticky pointers. Also add an automated canary test that simulates token-by-token streaming to catch regressions in tokens-to-first-byte.

Mira: I'll own adding the queue_wait_ms and kv_window_size panels. Alex, please paste the sweep config and I'll run the AB runner overnight.

Alex: Sweep config (running):
```
--prompt-set short_prompts_v2
--microbatch-sizes 4,8,12
--flush-ms 15,25,40
--chunk-tokens 8,16,32
--kernel-preference fused_int8,default
```

Alex: Will post results in ~2h. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
